rows.en: “So that tomorrow... you can be a slightly better person.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "For the sake... of becoming just a little better the next day."
Taichi: "I still have true companions."

rows.jp: 「築き上げることは、心を傷だらけにすることでもあります」
rows.en: “Building something can also leave the heart covered in wounds.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Building oneself up also means filling one's heart with wounds."

rows.jp: 「つらいばかりで、美しくないことです」
rows.en: “It is nothing but pain. There is no beauty in it.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "It is something merely painful, with no beauty to it."

rows.jp: 「でも人には人が、必要だと思いました」
rows.en: “But I have come to believe that people need other people.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But for a person, I thought, people are necessary."

rows.jp: 「だから、この放送を聞いている人もまだどこかにいると信じます」
rows.en: “So I believe there is still someone, somewhere, listening to this broadcast.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "That is why I believe there are still living people listening to this broadcast, somewhere."
Taichi: "Our address is---"

rows.jp: 無線連絡の際の手順も告げる。
rows.en: I also give the procedure for contacting us by radio.

ghs.en: I also announce the procedure to contact us via radio.
And this is all.

rows.jp: からっぽになるまで話せた、かな。
rows.en: I think I managed to talk until there was nothing left inside me.

ghs.en: I've talked until I was empty, have I.
...well, that's how it is.

rows.jp: 「こちら群青学院放送部、生存者は八名」
rows.en: “This is the Gunjo Academy Broadcasting Club. Eight survivors.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "This is the Gunjou Institute Broadcast Club, we have eight survivors."
Taichi: "See you next week."
Finished.

rows.en: I let out a long breath.

ghs.en: I take a rest with a sigh.
Applause.

rows.jp: まずみみ先輩。そして続いて他のみんな。

ghs.en: First was Mimi-senpai. Then everybody follows.
Taichi: "..."

rows.jp: 茶化す気にはならなかった。
rows.en: I do not feel like making a joke of it.

ghs.en: I couldn't bring myself to make fun of things.

rows.jp: 気恥ずかしさに包まれる。

ghs.en: I am engulfed by embarrassment.

rows.jp: その甘い拷問を耐えるため、俺は頬をかいた。
rows.en: To endure that sweet torture, I scratch my cheek.

ghs.en: I scratched my cheek to bear this sweet torture.
Misato: "Good, very well done!"
Taichi: "...huh."
Sakuraba: "Next week, you said?"
Taichi: "Ahhh, well... seemed appropriate."

rows.jp: 「いいんじゃないの。細かいことは」
rows.en: “Sounds fine. No need to worry about the details.”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "You sure it was right? All those details, I mean."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese reassures him that it is fine and dismisses the minor details. The English instead questions whether he was right and foregrounds those details, reversing the pragmatic force.
ghs.remedy: It's fine, isn't it? Don't sweat the details.

highlights.text: You sure it was right? All those details, I mean.

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "...don't they."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese is a brief agreement: 'Yeah' or 'Right.' The English is an incomplete negative tag question and does not express assent.

ghs.en: Miki: "You look'd so awesooome!"

rows.jp: 使い捨てカメラでバシバシ撮ってくる。
rows.en: She fires shot after shot with a disposable camera.

ghs.en: Click after click she was taking pictures with a disposable camera.
Taichi: "...c'mon stop iiit."
Miki: "Embarrassed! Embarrassed!"
Taichi: "Shaaaddeeeep!"
And then,
Kiri: "...Senpai."
Kiri stood.

rows.en: What is she going to say?

ghs.en: What will she even say?
I wait, tense.
Kiri: "Go."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese is only the initial syllable of the following formal acknowledgment, isolated as Kiri struggles to speak. Translating it as the imperative 'Go' invents lexical meaning and obscures the false start.

ghs.en: Go.
ghs.assessment: The narrator echoes Kiri's isolated opening syllable, not an imperative meaning 'go.' Assigning lexical meaning removes the mirrored hesitation.

ghs.en: Kiri: "Good... job out there."
A bow of the head.
Taichi: "......"

rows.en: A deep emotion wells up inside me.

ghs.en: A burst of strong feelings and deep emotions,

rows.en: I cannot put it into words.

ghs.en: that I cannot make into words.

rows.jp: 不可解な、それでいてほっとする、そんな感覚だ。

ghs.en: Something incomprehensible, yet at the same time a relief, a feeling like that.

rows.jp: 心の水位が増した気がする。
rows.en: It feels as though the water level in my heart has risen.

ghs.en: There's the feeling that the level of the water in my heart is rising,
an extremely small amount.
Taichi: "...thank ye."

rows.en: The sky pales for an instant.

ghs.en: The sky flashed white for an instant.
Taichi: "...!"

rows.jp: ああ、このタイミングか―――

ghs.en: Awww, it's gotta have this timing---
I quickly become terrified,

rows.jp: けど取り乱すわけにはいかない。

ghs.en: but I cannot afford to lose composure.
I hug Kiri.

rows.jp: 膝をついて、腹部に顔を埋める。
rows.en: I sink to my knees and bury my face against her stomach.

ghs.en: I fall to my knees, and bury my head in her belly.

rows.jp: 「きゃっ、ど、どうしたんですっ？」

ghs.en: Kiri: "Kyah, wh-, what do you think you're doing?!"
Miki: "Whoa, that's so bold..."
Misato: "I-, illicit sexual suspensionship..."
Sakuraba: "That's a neologism, President-senpai."
Tomoki: "...Taichi's really a perv innhe."

rows.jp: 「気が抜けたんじゃー！　慰めてくれー！」

ghs.en: Taichi: "I'm just exhausteeed! I'm being comforteeed!"
ghs.assessment: The Japanese is a request for Kiri to comfort him. The English turns it into a statement that the comforting is already happening.

ghs.en: Frightening.

rows.jp: 自分がなくなるのが恐ろしい。
rows.en: I am afraid of ceasing to exist.

ghs.en: That I will no longer be is frightening.

rows.jp: セーブは土曜の夜が最後。
rows.en: The last save was Saturday night.

ghs.en: Last save point was Saturday night.

rows.jp: 今日のこの喜びも懺悔も微量の心の成長も、全部無駄になる。
rows.en: Today's joy, this confession, the minute growth of my heart—all of it will be lost.

ghs.en: Today's happiness and repentance and the small amount of growth in the heart, too, will all be to waste.
I'm scared, scared, scared.
Kiri: "...Senpai... you're crying?"
Buzzing in the ears.

rows.jp: 胸に埋めた双眼の端、世界が白んでいく。
rows.en: With my face buried against her, the world grows white at the edges of my vision.

ghs.en: Near the edge of my eyes buried in the chest, the world was growing bright.
Growing bright---
Taichi: "...fuck me."

rows.jp: 往生際の言葉となった。

ghs.en: Those ended up being the last words before my end.
